text:
Maya (eng-infra): Quick follow-up from the incident postmortem — proposing a lightweight "egress fair-shed" interface to reduce head-of-line blocking when tenants spray lots of small egress calls. Goal: graceful fairness + clear hooks for product and runtime.

Jon: +1. We need to avoid penalizing high-SLO routes (realtime chat) vs. batch routes. Suggest SLO class tagging.

Priya: Idea: admission should attach two small hints: `egress_cost_est` (float tokens) and `slo_class` (enum: realtime | interactive | batch). Keep hints advisory only — egress scheduler makes the final decision.

Maya (eng-infra): Sketch of runtime behavior:
- Egress scheduler uses WFQ with per-slo-class weights.
- If tenant sustained rate exceeds a fast-path threshold -> apply soft-shed window (reduce allowed egress tokens for N seconds) rather than hard drop.
- Provide per-request floor token billing so noisy many-small-req SDKs don't game it.

Theo: Fast-path abuse detection should be simple and deterministic: if recent_rate > R and token_rate > T -> mark soft-shed. Don't wait for ML abuse_score for the immediate response.

Priya: Config proto snippet (informal):
```
egress_policy {
  scheduler: WFQ
  slo_weights: { realtime: 8, interactive: 2, batch: 1 }
  per_request_floor_tokens: 10
  fast_shed_thresholds: { rate_per_min: 1200, tokens_per_min: 50000 }
  probation_window_sec: 30
}
```

Jon: Tradeoffs: WFQ keeps fair throughput but can increase tail latency for realtime clients if weights wrong. Need a small latency boost mechanism: when `slo_class==realtime` bump weight temporarily when avg_wait_ms crosses a low threshold.

Maya (eng-infra): Telemetry we should emit for Console:
- tenant.egress.queue_len (gauge)
- tenant.egress.avg_wait_ms (histogram)
- tenant.egress.soft_shed_events (counter)
- tenant.egress.dropped_requests (counter)
- distribution of `egress_cost_est` attached by admission
- priority_override events with reason (e.g., failover, SLO bump)

Priya: Security note: hints must never be trusted for cross-tenant caching. Any `cache_hint` must be validated and caches remain tenant-scoped to avoid poisoning.

Theo: Fallbacks: before dropping, attempt transparent fallback routing so UX survives — e.g., route to quantized model variant or lower-cost region if latency allows.

Jon: Implementation nit: keep admission -> egress interface tiny: only `egress_cost_est`, `slo_class`, optional `cache_hint`. All numeric values are advisory and clamped by egress-side policy.

Maya (eng-infra): I'll draft a short RFC with exact proto, smoothing windows (10s fast window + 5m smoothing), and telemetry panels. Planning a canary for prod-eu next week.

SRE Bot: Canary job created: infra/egress-fair-shed-v1 -> canary prod-eu 2024-06-12 09:00 UTC :rocket:

DevOps Bot: FYI deploy note: ensure feature-flag gating and rollback path included in runbook.

Maya (eng-infra): Thanks — will link RFC here once ready. Quick ask: reviewers focus on edge cases where clients intentionally send tiny requests to drive cost and on interactions with KV cache hits.
